related_resources.reason: Abstract states material (absolute/relative), formal, style/genre, and process taxonomy; discusses voluntary/received limits. No claim to have read full chapter.
Book identification and exercise-based format; not treated as proving constraints always improve outcomes.
Foreword contrasts if-then rule with interdependent constraints; foreword not asserted to be authored by Variego.
Abstract presents combination, exploration, transformation and difficulty of evaluation versus generation. No empirical appraisal of this lecture or modern music AI.
Author distinguishes composing by a procedure from audibly perceptible gradual processes. This original lesson is not a Reich process composition.
Reich reflects that his 1968 essay described previous practice and was not a future manifesto.
Supports historical description of Cage, chance operations, indeterminacy; historical framing is not a universal method.
Describes Cage’s I Ching mappings and chance operations; useful corroboration for historical method and distinction.
Acoustic, notated, perceived repetitions and functions of repetition are in abstract; no listening data for these particular scores.
Abstract connects repeated material with attention in time; not a direct test of this course’s arrangements.
Seeded pseudorandom sequences; reproducing exact draws requires this pack’s documented Python call semantics and stored choices.
Describes import of prerecorded audio; not independent evidence of listening outcomes.
Documented optional audio-processing workflow. Pack’s executable renderer uses standard library instead.

claim_evidence.anchor: A rule can change that.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Opening pedagogical proposal, not experimentally established to improve originality.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Hasegawa, publisher abstract: constraints as creative framework

claim_evidence.anchor: These are four different dimensions of musical constraint.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Hasegawa abstract explicitly identifies four classes: material, formal, style/genre, process.

claim_evidence.anchor: The music theorist Robert Hasegawa makes a related four-part distinction
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Specific scholarly attribution of fourfold classification.

claim_evidence.anchor: The second says: the final phrase must recall the beginning.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original illustration of formal versus pitch-material constraint; no experimental claim.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Lecture 042000, invented paired instructions; Hasegawa taxonomy contextual

claim_evidence.anchor: A hard constraint has a checkable condition
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Operational distinction authored for course; not attributed as direct Hasegawa terminology.

claim_evidence.anchor: A computer can check the first kind from symbolic data.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Score event checks can establish chosen formal conditions but cannot verify listener evaluations.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Local score validator; Python docs for deterministic computation

claim_evidence.anchor: Twelve identical returns might be a compositional failure in one work and the exact point of another.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Context-dependent artistic interpretation, not a result about a tested score.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Margulis, Repetition, abstract: functions of recurrence vary

claim_evidence.anchor: Every version is in four-quarter meter, at one hundred quarter-note beats per minute.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Shared declared tempo and meter across 8 pieces; external source only contextual.

claim_evidence.anchor: Every version begins with the same four quarter notes, E, G, A, G.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Exact opening lead events validated across all eight versions.

claim_evidence.anchor: The same simple oscillators, source gains, and stereo settings are assigned to corresponding voices.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Cross-piece voice configurations compared in local checker; differing density can affect perceived loudness.

claim_evidence.anchor: That four-bar pattern is repeated four times.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Bass event list repeats four-bar cycle 4 times, with two notes per measure.

claim_evidence.anchor: But this is not a controlled psychological experiment.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Audio comparison does not control perception, timbre, or conduct listeners trials.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Lecture methodology limitation; Margulis does not test our stimuli

claim_evidence.anchor: the five pitch classes C, D, E, G, and A.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Checker enforces the set on all 64 notes of closed-palette lead.

claim_evidence.anchor: For the first eight bars, nothing changes.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Lead pairs have no changed events until bar 10; shared accompaniment fixed.

claim_evidence.anchor: There are exactly four changed note events in the whole sixteen-bar melody
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Changed events at bar10 beat3, bar11 beat1, bar14 beat2, bar15 beat3, one semitone each.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Score: pitch_changed_events and comparison of palette leads

claim_evidence.anchor: The bass and inner voice do not change.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Literal companion voice event arrays held fixed in all eight versions.

claim_evidence.anchor: The third version keeps every lead attack on a numbered beat.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Rhythm grid starts four one-beat notes at integer offsets in each bar.

claim_evidence.anchor: The first eight bars are identical to the regular version.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Rhythm versions have same first 32 lead events.

claim_evidence.anchor: The second note begins on the offbeat after beat two, and the fourth begins on the offbeat after beat four.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: After midpoint, lead attacks at bar offsets 1.5 and 3.5 beats, .5 durations.

claim_evidence.anchor: The fifth version adds a follower to the original melody.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Fourth voice present only in echo pair; same lead/bass/inner.

claim_evidence.anchor: every note in the lead is repeated one full measure later, an octave lower.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Follower = all lead events before bar16, at+4 beats and pitch octave lowered; beyond piece omitted.

claim_evidence.anchor: It is not a certification that every simultaneous interval satisfies an eighteenth-century counterpoint exercise.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Local checker tests delay and transposition, no detailed contrapuntal style analysis.

claim_evidence.anchor: in bars eleven and twelve, where eight separate quarter-note entries would otherwise occur, the follower uses four two-beat notes instead.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Strict 8 quarter events replaced by 4 half events only at beats40..47; no outside changes.

claim_evidence.anchor: Most of the follower remains an exact delayed octave copy.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Outside bars11-12 the event arrays are identical.

claim_evidence.anchor: a bank of six four-note melodic gestures.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Six original candidate arrays, each four quarter notes.

claim_evidence.anchor: For each of the remaining fifteen bars, a pseudorandom generator chooses one of the six gestures.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: random.Random(seed).randrange(6) exactly once each for bars2..16; bar1 fixed.

claim_evidence.anchor: We record its seed, forty-two thousand.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Seed explicitly stored as 42000 with choices.

claim_evidence.anchor: A pseudorandom draw is not an unrepeatable physical event.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Python documentation describes pseudorandom generation from deterministic state and seeding.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Python docs, Bookkeeping functions and Notes on Reproducibility

claim_evidence.anchor: the raw draw, exactly as selected.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Score raw lead must match candidate bank indexed by stored draws.

claim_evidence.anchor: in exactly three measures: eight, twelve, and sixteen.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Three authored replacements in score map; validator enforces exact bars and changed candidate IDs.

claim_evidence.anchor: the revised line uses D, E, G, C instead of the original draw's D, F, E, D.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Raw choice 3 at bar16; replacement choice5 at bar16.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Score: draw candidates and indices for last bar

claim_evidence.anchor: John Cage used chance operations in a way that could deliberately displace the composer's taste
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Pardo discusses Cage using chance to step back from habitual aesthetic choices.
claim_evidence.source_locator: IRCAM profile, section II paragraphs on I Ching and compositional responsibility

claim_evidence.anchor: It should not be described as a realization of Cage's philosophy
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Explicit distinction: controlled composer-picked bank and after-the-fact edits serve different purpose.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Haskins, review discussion of Cage chance operations

claim_evidence.anchor: a chance procedure used to *compose a fixed score* from indeterminacy left for a *performance*.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Distinguishes composition-time selection vs performance-time choices, though practices can overlap.
claim_evidence.source_locator: IRCAM profile, section II; Haskins review

claim_evidence.anchor: Jorge Variego's *Composing with Constraints* is expressly organized around practical exercises
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Published title and book description explicitly describe 100 practical exercises.

claim_evidence.anchor: Its publisher's foreword contrasts a simple rule with a larger system of interacting conditions
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: OUP Foreword extract contrasts if-then rules with interacting conditions.

claim_evidence.anchor: Margaret Boden's work on computational creativity distinguishes combining existing ideas
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Abstract distinguishes combinational, exploratory and transformational generation.

claim_evidence.anchor: generating candidates is not the same as evaluating them.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Abstract explicitly notes evaluation is more difficult than generation.

claim_evidence.anchor: Steve Reich makes a distinction in his 1968 essay *Music as a Gradual Process*.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Primary essay specifies audible processes distinct from writing with a process.

claim_evidence.anchor: the listener can perceive as they happen.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Reich specifically states interest in perceptible processes.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Reich, Music as a Gradual Process

claim_evidence.anchor: Reich later cautioned against treating his 1968 essay as a manifesto
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Author preface explicitly says essay described work up to 1968 and was not future manifesto.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Reich, Writings on Music, Author’s Preface

claim_evidence.anchor: The distinction between acoustic, notated, and *perceived* repetition is also important.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Margulis abstract explicitly distinguishes acoustic/notated/perceived repetition.

claim_evidence.anchor: Elizabeth Hellmuth Margulis has analyzed these as distinct aspects of musical repetition
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Author attribution and described focus appear in abstract.

claim_evidence.anchor: It does not detect what a listener treats as a return.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Score equality and perceptual similarity are not the same measurement; no human listeners tested.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Score validator limitations; Margulis distinguishes score and perception

claim_evidence.anchor: Use the same bar range and the same monitoring chain.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original recommended listening protocol, not claimed as standardized perceptual experiment.

claim_evidence.anchor: We can use Ardour to align the same passages for comparison
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Ardour manual supports importing media; local workflow recommendation not automatically an ABX protocol.

claim_evidence.anchor: we can render the note events with alternative patches in DawDreamer
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: DawDreamer offline plugin graph allows alternate instrument or processing choices; not implemented in the standard-library pack script.
claim_evidence.source_locator: DawDreamer user guide, plugins and rendering

claim_evidence.anchor: A test for a motif returning at bar twelve is meaningful.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Can be checked from MIDI/note events, but cannot prove artistic merit.

claim_evidence.anchor: The log says: the melody stayed within five pitch classes;
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Examples summarizing the verified four paired comparisons.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Score: all versions and pair metadata

claim_evidence.anchor: Not call-and-response. Not exact canonic imitation.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: No universal structural prescription follows from typology or examples.

description: Compares composing with pitch constraints, chance procedures, and other imposed rules, asking when a constraint clarifies artistic judgment and when it traps the music.
